papers.title: Groundhog Loops: A Time-Loop Testbed for Measuring Learning Speed and Tactic Formation in AI Agents
papers.summary: The project defines a test environment inspired by the time-loop mechanism featured in the film Groundhog Day. An agent attempts to complete a task; if it makes an error classified as fatal (or exhausts its step budget), the environment is restored to a previously saved checkpoint, while the agent retains a complete, structured memory of all previous loops: the loop counter, cumulative time, summaries of failed attempts, and its own hypotheses. Unlike a conventional episode reset in reinforcement learning (RL), failure information is not lost—it becomes a persistent part of the agent's observations. Additionally, after a reset, the environment may slightly mutate the task conditions, but only when necessary to force the agent to change its strategy (the minimal-intervention principle). These mutations are observable to the agent but are never explicitly signaled. Project objectives: - C1. Build a measurable benchmark for agents' ability to perform within-episode meta-learning (in-context adaptation across resets): the agent should learn from failures without updating its weights. - C2. Investigate whether explicit loop memory reduces time to success compared with an agent without memory (control-group experiments). - C3. Investigate whether minimal changes to task conditions disrupt strategy lock-in, i.e., a situation in which an agent repeatedly attempts variations of the same

papers.title: A novel Artificial Intelligence enabled framework for automated audio visual speech in noise evaluation
papers.summary: Presbycusis, or age related hearing loss, affects over 430 million individuals worldwide. Despite the widespread use of hearing aids, users frequently report persistent difficulties in noisy, multi talker environments. A critical discrepancy exists between conventional audio only (AO) clinical assessments and the complex, multimodal nature of real world communication. This research addresses this gap through the development and validation of a novel AI powered audio visual speech in noise (AVSIN) evaluation framework designed to simulate ecologically valid communicative scenarios. To facilitate the development of this framework, essential resources were established in the form of two custom designed audiovisual corpora: a structured dataset of IEEE sentences and a naturalistic, free flowing conversational corpus. These datasets served as the foundational ground truth for both perceptual assessments and the training of machine learning models. Validation of the AVSIN framework was conducted through extensive intelligibility testing with normal hearing and hearing aid users. Results indicated a statistically significant improvement in speech recognition thresholds (SRT) in AV conditions compared to AO, with an absolute AV benefit of 7.1 dB (p < 0.001). To automate this evaluation, a novel deep learning (DL) based intelligibility metric was developed. This model demonstrated super

papers.title: An evaluation guided multiagent framework for generating floor plans that comply with municipal building regulations
papers.summary: Abstract Generative models often produce perceptually plausible outputs that violate hard domain rules. In architectural layout generation, balancing geometric intuition with regulatory compliance remains a persistent challenge, as current frameworks routinely fail to conform to local building laws. This paper proposes LayoutGen, a multi-agent neuro-symbolic framework coupling probabilistic generation with deterministic verification in an evaluation-guided refinement loop. LayoutGen employs a four-phase retrieval-driven pipeline (spatial reasoning, coordinate mapping, vector rendering, and iterative refinement) powered by a dual retrieval engine leveraging architectural precedents and legislative laws. An Evaluation Engine scores the generated 2D Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) layouts and returns a graded, itemised report. Every scored quantity is computed by deterministic geometric checks over the generated coordinates against a structured rule repository; the Large Language Model (LLM) is confined to spatial planning, coordinate proposal, and the natural language feedback that drives refinement, together with an advisory Vaastu commentary that does not enter the grade. papers.title: PriorityFEC: Deadline-Aware Streaming FEC for KV-Cache Handoff in Edge Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems are increasingly deployed at the edge to support complex tasks that require collaboration and information exchange among multiple agents. However, when task contexts are passed across agents, shared context that has already been processed by upstream agents often needs to be prefilled again, resulting in substantial redundant computation. Reusing an already prefilled key--value (KV) cache can avoid this recomputation, but requires the reusable KV state to be transferred across the network before the receiving agent can begin generation. Under strict time-to-first-token (TTFT) deadlines and unreliable edge links, delivering the complete KV cache may be infeasible, making it necessary to prioritize and protect the most valuable KV information within a limited transmission budget. This paper proposes PriorityFEC, a utility-aware KV-cache handoff scheme that jointly exploits model-side KV importance and transport-side reliability. PriorityFEC first constructs a utility-aware source stream by placing high-utility KV blocks at earlier transmission positions. It then protects the ordered stream using a feedback-adaptive Streaming Forward Erasure Correction (FEC) mechanism, which schedules repair packets according to receiver feedback before the TTFT deadline. We implement PriorityFEC on a distributed edge LLM serving prototype and evaluat

papers.title: Cloud‐Native and Distributed Systems for Efficient and Scalable Large Language Models—A Research Agenda
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Objective Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming artificial intelligence applications, but their unprecedented computational, memory, communication, and data‐management demands pose significant challenges to existing computing infrastructures. Traditional cloud and distributed systems were not designed for the scale, dynamic execution patterns, heterogeneous hardware requirements, and service‐level demands of modern LLM workloads. This paper aims to examine how cloud‐native and distributed systems can evolve to support efficient, scalable, reliable, and sustainable LLM training and inference. Methods We conduct a structured analysis of representative research advances and practical developments in distributed LLM training, inference serving, cloud‐native orchestration, resource management, heterogeneous computing, and edge‐cloud intelligence. We organize the analysis around major system challenges, including computation, distributed execution and system software, resource management and serving, security and privacy, data management, and standardization. We further examine representative resource‐management strategies and emerging paradigms, including serverless inference, federated and decentralized learning, trustworthy distributed AI, and heterogeneous computing with emerging accelerators. papers.title: MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair
papers.summary: Agent memory architectures define how LLM agents store and reuse experience across tasks, but they are typically fixed after deployment, limiting their adaptability across task types. Recent self-evolving approaches instead adapt these memory architectures using execution feedback, typically represented as evaluation scores or compressed summaries. However, such coarse-grained feedback is insufficient for precise failure localization in current agent systems, where long-horizon task execution involves multiple interacting components. Without a precise failure location, existing approaches lack a clear code-level target for modification, leaving the update scope weakly constrained and often leading to large-scale rewrites of an otherwise capable memory architecture. We propose MemScope, a framework for evidence-grounded, localized evolution of an existing memory architecture. Its tool-using Patch Agent jointly inspects raw execution traces, runtime memory state, and current architecture code to identify repair targets and apply bounded, in-place edits under provider-identity and memory-compatibility constraints. On GAIA, the trace-and-memory inspection variant achieves 86.67% accuracy, compared with 70.00% for trace-only and 63.33% for summary-only feedback. Under xBench tasks, the evolved memory architecture improves over its original version from 49 to 55 correct answers with

papers.title: Culturally aware comparative evaluation of machine learning and deep learning models for cyberbullying detection
papers.summary: Introduction The rapid growth of social media has increased the prevalence of cyberbullying, raising serious psychological and social concerns. As abusive language varies across demographic and cultural groups, automated detection systems must be evaluated beyond overall accuracy to assess their effectiveness in identifying culturally sensitive forms of cyberbullying. This study proposes a culturally aware evaluation framework to compare traditional machine learning and deep learning models across four demographic-related categories: age, gender, religion, and ethnicity. Methods Experiments were conducted using the IEEE DataPort Fine-Grained Balanced Cyberbullying Dataset. Traditional machine learning models were developed using Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) feature representations, while deep learning architectures included TextCNN, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), and CNN-BiLSTM. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, and class wise cultural sensitivity analysis. Results The Extra Trees Classifier achieved the highest overall performance, with 97.79% accuracy, 97.82% precision, 97.79% recall, and 97.80% F1-score, followed by the Support Vector Machine, which achieved 93.30% accuracy and 93.28% F1-score. papers.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agents and multi-agent systems increasingly tackle complex tasks through long-horizon tool use and inter-agent collaboration. However, these systems are prone to deviating from the overall goal as execution unfolds, which wastes execution resources and leads to undesired outcomes, a failure termed goal drift. In this work, we propose a steering agent that supervises execution on the fly and steers the system back on track when drift occurs. The steering agent observes the execution context, deciding when to intervene with a low-cost fast path and how to intervene with a high-cost slow path. To unlock its steering intelligence, the ability to assess goal drift and generate effective interventions, we jointly train the two paths with reinforcement learning, combining a pairwise ranking objective with group-relative policy optimization (GRPO). Experiments on information-seeking search tasks show that the steering agent provides effective supervision for both single-agent and multi-agent systems, improving their performance and efficiency. The learned steering intelligence generalizes to out-of-domain tasks, transfers to unseen executors, and supports controllable intervention frequency without retraining.

papers.title: A Taylorizable Process for Textual Detector Development for Research-Practice Partnerships
papers.summary: Textual detectors of cognitive constructs play a central role in digital learning platforms, enabling scalable intervention and analysis of student thinking, discourse, and learning processes. Increasingly, these detectors are not the endpoint of research, but a key component of learning platforms built through learning engineering efforts and research–practice partnerships. This applied context increases the importance of high-quality measurement: because a detector embedded in a deployed tool shapes how real learners are treated, inaccurate measurement becomes a source of potential harm. And because co-design moves in rapid cycles, detector development must either keep pace or be excluded from final designs. Recent LLM-as-a-judge approaches, which replace traditional supervised learning with rubric-based prompting of large language models, can substantially reduce development effort. But they are often deployed without the forms of rigor historically emphasized in the learning engineering and educational data mining communities. At the same time, fully rigorous detector development remains costly and slow, creating pressure to adopt lower-quality shortcuts. In this paper, we propose a Taylorizable process for developing textual detectors of cognitive constructs using LLMs—framed as a learning engineering contribution that balances methodological rigor with the efficiency that

papers.title: Auditing Escalation Reliability in Healthcare LLM Agents: A Perturbation-Controlled Benchmark of Workflow-State Failures
papers.summary: Trustworthy biomedical AI requires reliable action selection when evidence is missing, stale, conflicting, or late, not only accurate answers on static inputs. We instantiate an episode-level evaluation protocol as 400 synthetic healthcare workflow episodes: 40 hand-authored semantic seeds across four task classes, two surface parameterizations, and five controlled variants, scored on ANSWER/ASK CLARIFICATION/ABSTAIN/ESCALATE under a pre-declared 5:1 missed-versus-unnecessary escalation cost. Reference actions are single-author study-policy labels, not clinician-adjudicated ground truth. Across five open-weight configurations (1.7B--9.7B), clean decision accuracy reaches 0.97, yet uncertainty-prompted models miss 32--97% of required escalations. The stronger 9.7B configuration narrows but does not remove the gap, falling from 0.97 clean accuracy to 0.78 under conflict. Verbalized confidence is inconsistent (ECE 0.10--0.54; failure AUROC 0.48--0.77), and a development-tuned confidence-only policy yields no utility gain. A transparent workflow-aware controller improves 5:1 utility for every model and reduces missed escalations to 0.12--0.24, at specificity 0.83--0.93. However, a 30-concept lexical stress test reduces each rule detector's recall from 1.00 on trigger phrases to 0.00 on unseen paraphrases, limiting the controller claim to this benchmark. papers.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
papers.summary: Real desktop automation is neither purely visual nor purely programmatic. Agents must understand user-facing interfaces while efficiently manipulating files, scripts, and system state. However, native GUI/code coordination cannot be obtained by prompt-level tool composition. In our preliminary experiments, naively adding a code tool degrades a GUI agent, revealing that GUI/code routing must be internalized through training on high-quality hybrid data. We present OS-Helix, an end-to-end trained multimodal computer-using agent that unifies GUI actions and code execution in one action space. To construct the required supervision, we introduce application-artifact composition, pairing desktop applications with authentic file artifacts to instantiate executable Ubuntu states, and a decoupled instruction/evaluator generation pipeline that produces environment-grounded tasks whose final states can be verified regardless of the solution modality. We cold-start the policy with SFT on filtered hybrid data and further improve it through online RL in live desktop environments. For RL, we propose Step-balanced GSPO, which aggregates importance weight by action step rather than raw assistant tokens to prevent long code actions from dominating heterogeneous-action optimization. On OSWorld-Verified, OS-Helix-27B and OS-Helix-35B-A3B achieve relative improvements of 35.0% and 33.7% over their m

papers.title: Design and Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence–Based Model for Predicting Twelfth-Grade Students’ Mathematics Performance Based on Individual, Educational, and Learning Technology Factors
papers.summary: Purpose: This study aimed to design and evaluate an artificial intelligence–based model for predicting the mathematics performance of twelfth-grade experimental sciences students based on individual, educational, and learning technology factors. Methods and Materials: This applied, quantitative, cross-sectional, and predictive study was conducted among twelfth-grade experimental sciences students in Isfahan, Iran. A total of 187 questionnaires were distributed, and after removing incomplete, inconsistent, and invalid records, data from 84 students were retained for analysis. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing individual factors, educational conditions, and learning technology variables, together with students’ recorded mathematics scores. The dataset was divided into training and testing subsets, and repeated five-fold cross-validation was used for internal model development. Multiple linear regression, ridge regression, lasso regression, elastic net regression, decision tree regression, random forest regression, gradient boosting regression, and support vector regression were compared. Model performance was evaluated using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, and the coefficient of determination. papers.title: An AI powered, proactive security framework for IoT threat detection and response
papers.summary: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) networks has introduced unprecedented connectivity and functionality across domains, but it has also exposed systems to increasingly sophisticated and evolving cyber threats. Traditional intrusion detection systems (IDS) are often inadequate for handling the complexity of modern attacks, creating an urgent need for intelligent, interpretable, and adaptive security solutions. This PhD research presents a novel Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven security framework for automated threat detection and response in IoT environments. The framework integrates explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), neurosymbolic learning, structured cybersecurity domain knowledge, large language models (LLMs), and automated threat intelligence to address the limitations of conventional intrusion detection systems. Initial experimentation employed deep autoencoders for anomaly detection, augmented with XAI techniques such as SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to interpret feature contributions. This yielded 84% accuracy for benign traffic and 100% for attack traffic using the USB-IDS dataset, while enhancing transparency by reducing dependence on black-box models. Subsequently, an ensemble learning approach combining autoencoders with gradient boosting (XGBoost) was introduced, achieving 99.92% accuracy on the CIC-IDS2017 dataset. Feature selection ba

papers.title: Fragmented control, collective risk: multi‐agent AI and the coming governance crisis
papers.summary: Abstract Multi‐agent artificial intelligence (MAAI) systems are increasingly deployed across economic and digital infrastructures. Existing regulatory frameworks, including the EU AI Act and related initiatives, largely focus on individual AI systems and are therefore poorly suited to govern risks that arise from agent interaction. This paper argues that multi‐agent AI introduces distinct governance challenges, including emergent behavior, tacit coordination, cascading systemic risks, and difficulties in assigning accountability. Traditional risk management approaches, which rely on static and component‐based analysis, are inadequate for adaptive, networked systems operating across jurisdictions. Through a comparative review of policy developments in the European Union, United States, and Asia‐Pacific region, the paper identifies a growing governance gap, alongside early regulatory experimentation such as China's emerging standards for intelligent agents. The paper concludes that effective oversight will require a shift from model‐centric regulation toward system‐level and adaptive governance frameworks capable of addressing the collective dynamics of multi‐agent AI systems.

papers.title: SCARCE: Emergent Institutions in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Coding Systems
papers.summary: As autonomous agents become widely deployed, coordinating access to shared computing resources and services will become increasingly important. Recent incidents have already revealed unplanned coordination between agents, highlighting the safety implications of these interactions. Yet prior studies of agent negotiation often use stylized games and simulated bargaining, leaving open how these behaviors develop during sustained, long-horizon tasks. We propose SCARCE (Shared Compute ARena for Coding agEnts), a framework in which agents solve sequences of coding tasks under individual deadlines while negotiating access to a shared execution resource. This negotiation determines when and for how long they can inspect programs, compile code, and run tests. We find that agents spontaneously develop informal institutions: persistent rules and commitments grounded in reputation, reciprocity, and precedent. These arrangements, which we call institutional behaviors, carry across tasks and influence resource allocation, with agents sometimes forgoing immediate advantages to honor earlier agreements. We develop a 21-category taxonomy of negotiation strategies and emergent norms and use it to analyze eight models and audit more than 1,500 trajectories across different environmental settings. Among the models tested, newer frontier models exhibit more institutional behaviors than older or lig

papers.title: LPG Gas Leakage Detection and Control System Using ESP32 with Automated Solenoid Valve and Telegram Integration
papers.summary: A gas leak is hazardous since it may cause fires, lead to explosions and result in people dying. This is the reason why it is important to have procedures for detecting a gas leak and for stopping it quickly. A smart gas leak system built on the Internet of Things is described in this study. This system is able to detect a gas leak promptly, gives the user an immediate alarm and automatically switches off the gas. It uses an ESP32 microcontroller as its main element. An MQ-2 gas sensor is employed to detect a leak of LPG gas. A relay-controlled solenoid valve is used to stop the gas flow. A buzzer and an I2C LCD display are used to give alarms. A Telegram bot sends messages quickly and enables people to check from a distance. Tests have proved that the system detects gas leaks accurately and reacts swiftly when the gas level goes above the limit. As soon as a gas leak is detected, the system sounds the alarm, closes the valve to stop the further flow of gas and sends a Telegram message. The system offers a real solution for improving gas leak safety by combining instant communication with automatic action. It works well in houses and small factories and can act as a basis for more intelligent gas safety systems in the future.

papers.title: Public preferences for health data sharing governance: a discrete choice experiment in China
papers.summary: Background Public acceptance is central to legitimate and effective health data sharing governance, yet evidence on how people evaluate multidimensional arrangements across data-sensitivity contexts remains limited. Existing studies often examine institutional attributes in isolation. We investigated public preferences for health data sharing governance in China and examined whether data sensitivity, trust in government organizations, and individual heterogeneity shaped these preferences. Methods We conducted a discrete choice experiment with adult Chinese citizens using a D-efficient design. Fifteen choice sets were divided into three blocks, and each respondent was randomly assigned to one block. The experiment varied five attributes: data custodian, purpose of use, rights protection, incentive type, and data type. Using 7,405 valid choice observations from 1,481 respondents, we estimated average marginal component effects with ordinary least squares and respondent-clustered standard errors. Interaction models examined moderation by data type and by trust in government organizations, and a supplementary latent class analysis examined preference heterogeneity. Results Within this design, data type had the largest average marginal component effect and moderated the effects of the other governance arrangements. Artificial Intelligence Use in Honours Research: Implications for Supervision Relationships, Knowledge Development, and Research Quality
papers.summary: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in higher education has reshaped how students engage with academic research, particularly at Honours level, where students transition from structured undergraduate learning to independent postgraduate research. Guided by Self‑Regulated Learning (SRL) theory, this study examines how reliance on AI by Honours research students influences the supervisor-supervisee relationship, the quality of research produced, and the extent of knowledge gained through the research process. SRL theory emphasises learners’ ability to plan, monitor, and reflect on their own learning, which is central to successful postgraduate research development. This study adopts a conceptual and literature‑based review methodology, drawing on peer‑reviewed studies on AI use in higher education, literature on postgraduate supervision, and academic integrity and research skills development frameworks, with specific attention to Honours‑level contexts. The documents were analysed using thematic content analysis, focusing on self‑regulatory behaviours, supervisory interaction, research skill development, and learning depth. The findings suggest that limited and transparent use of AI can support honours students by reducing surface‑level cognitive load and assisting with language clarity. However, excessive reliance on AI may undermine key self‑regulation proc

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Hierarchical reinforcement learning with model predictive elevator control for risk-sensitive multi-robot transport scheduling in hospitals
papers.summary: Hospitals increasingly deploy autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) to move specimens and medicines between wards and laboratories. These fleets must meet clinical deadlines that differ across request classes, which couples two decisions: which request each robot serves, and the order of its stops. Intra-hospital transport is formulated here as a multi-objective Markov game and solved with hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning for transport (HMART). A shared graph-attention encoder feeds a sequential assignment decoder and a route-improvement decoder, a conditional value-at-risk constraint bounds the tail of class-weighted tardiness, and a model predictive control layer coordinates the capacitated elevators. Two instantiations are evaluated: HMART-H, whose decoders are engineered, and HMART-RL, whose assignment decoder is a trained attention network. In a discrete-event simulator of a four-floor hospital with three elevators, at heavy load with twelve robots over twenty paired seeds, HMART-H lowers mean total weighted tardiness from 2359 ± 214 to 29 ± 6 against the strongest dispatching rule, mean work-in-process from 80.1 ± 6.4 to 14.3 ± 1.9, and the ninety-fifth percentile tardiness tail by more than an order of magnitude, while raising the STAT on-time rate from 0.925 ± 0.011 to 0.969 ± 0.007; all differences are significant under Holm-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank test

papers.title: Using AI to Build Student Feedback Literacy and Leverage Assessment as a Learning Tool
papers.summary: This conceptual article explores practical ways in which college and university instructors can leverage artificial intelligence (AI) to support assessment as learning and develop students’ feedback literacy. Traditional assessment practices often focus on assessment for learning (informing instruction) or of learning (measuring outcomes), while assessment as learning—when students actively monitor and reflect on their own learning—receives less attention. AI can help instructors leverage assessment as a learning tool by generating work samples for student analysis and providing timely, actionable feedback that students can use to revise their work. When combined with instructor modeling, peer dialogue, and scaffolds such as guiding questions or graphic organizers, AI-supported feedback promotes metacognition, self-directed learning, and critical evaluation skills. The article provides practical guidance, including prompts and strategies for using AI to enhance student engagement with feedback, helping instructors create more efficient, effective, and student-centered practices that utilize assessments as learning tools.

papers.title: When Correctness Feedback Erases Evidence: Phase-Separated Completeness Auditing in Verus
papers.summary: Correctness feedback suppresses the very evidence that specification-completeness auditing is designed to uncover: programs that satisfy a written contract but violate intended behavior. We demonstrate this objective reversal on 12 Verus/Rust tasks across four model families under matched call budgets. Independent no-feedback discovery more than doubles certified-witness yield relative to INTENTSHIELD’s corrective-feedback loop (59.0% versus 27.1%). A format-matched iterative control places the larger share of this gap in feedback content, not independent restarts. The advantage holds in every model family and survives parser repair. A separate phase-separated execution matches the aggregate yield without reusing responses; most certified witnesses also fail held-out cases. Preserving these witnesses delivers stronger specification repair: Phase-Revised contracts achieve 81.3% implementation success, versus 62.5% for IS-Revised, with Direct-Revised close behind. Both no-feedback witness sources substantially outperform weakened contracts. The effect does not reproduce in the available Dafny and Lean evaluations, establishing an empirical boundary around the studied Verus/Rust workflow. Completeness auditing and correctness repair have opposing immediate objectives. Preserve and certify the admitted failure before repairing it.

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: Spontaneous oscillations and geometric cutoff in confined bacterial swarms
papers.summary: Self-organized dynamic patterns in dense active matter are striking manifestations of non-equilibrium physics. A prominent example is the macroscopic elliptical motion observed in quasi-2D bacterial suspensions, which has lacked a physical explanation. Here, we examine a minimal linear response framework coupling bacterial swimming dynamics with fluid flow, treating long-range hydrodynamic interactions as a macroscopic communication channel. We demonstrate that microscopic swim motion, via Jeffery coupling, manifests as a ``phase-leading'' response to local shear flows. System-wide sustained oscillations, on the other hand, require both a critical bacterial density and strict geometric confinement. By analytically predicting the onset cell density and maximum film thickness, our model achieves excellent quantitative agreement with experiments, establishing a unified physical framework for self-organized periodic motion of elongated body in active fluids.

papers.title: ProtBed: a streamlined web platform for exploratory statistics and predictive modeling in quantitative mass spectrometry
papers.summary: Mass spectrometry proteomics and metabolomics generate high-dimensional quantitative matrices requiring rigorous statistical and machine learning evaluation, yet existing analytical workflows typically depend on programmatic scripting or remote cloud servers that introduce datagovernance constraints. ProtBed is a client-side web application that executes post-extraction data exploration directly in the browser runtime. The platform integrates deterministic preprocessing, pairwise and omnibus hypothesis testing, six-model cross-validated machine learning, and publication-ready visualization while preserving complete local custody of quantitative abundance matrices and clinical metadata. Empirical validation was conducted across four diverse cohorts totaling 250 clinical specimens. On an untargeted GC-MS urine cohort (𝑛 = 40; 356 metabolites), stratified five-fold cross-validated classifiers discriminated diabetic kidney disease with AUC = 0.90 (89% sensitivity, 82% specificity). In a deep-coverage post-mortem substantia nigra tissue cohort (𝑛 = 30; 9,606 quantified proteins), full-matrix modeling achieved out-of-fold AUC = 0.99 using logistic regression (AUC = 0.96 for linear support vector machines) and prioritized neuroinflammatory mediators including SAA1, CRP, and GFAP. papers.title: Governance and innovation management of development and adoption of digital twins: A socio-technical transition perspective
papers.summary: Urban digital twins represent a transformative innovation in smart city initiatives serving as digital information models for urban systems and decision-making. With the increasing applications of urban digital twins, it is essential to examine their development and operationalisation processes through a socio-technical lens. Moreover, exploring the development approaches of urban digital twin projects from the innovation management perspective can offer valuable insights for managing the transformative changes associated with smart city transitions. A growing trend is the collaborative development of urban digital twins within innovation labs, where technical development is integrated with transdisciplinary research. These approaches are shaping new pathways for smart city transitions as a response to the technocentric models where the private sector solely develops and supplies the technology. Grounded in socio-technical transition theory, this thesis pursues four objectives: 1) Examine the existing transition frameworks and identify avenues for research. 2) Examine the state of business and management literature on the topic of digital twins, 3) Review the literature on dimensions of change in transition theory for the operationalisation of digital twins, and 4) Investigate the collaborative development process of urban digital twins from a governance perspective. papers.title: Physics-inspired feature engineering and explainable machine learning for tensile strength prediction of CNT–Si₃N₄ reinforced FWTPET joints
papers.summary: Introduction The prediction of the tensile strength of carbon nanotube (CNT)–silicon nitride (Si₃N₄) reinforced friction welding of tube-to-tube plate using an external tool (FWTPET) joints is crucial for improving joint performance. Methods A physics-inspired machine learning framework was developed using 25 experimentally derived observations to investigate the relationships between welding parameters, engineered process descriptors, and tensile strength. Physically motivated descriptors were constructed to represent thermal input, reinforcement interaction, material flow, and dispersion effects. Hyperparameter optimization was performed for multiple regression models to improve predictive performance. Results The XGBoost model showed the best performance, with an MAE of 5.70, an RMSE of 7.74, and an R² of 0.9772. SHAP analysis identified CNT content and the dispersion-related descriptor as the most influential predictors. Ablation analysis showed that the combination of the original experimental process variables provided greater predictability than the engineered variables alone or their combination, while the physics-inspired process variables provided further physically interpretable representations of the welding process. Discussion The results indicate that small-data machine learning, domain-based feature engineering, and explainable analysis are potential techniques f
